answer: A slow-identity gate can blunt Sybil attacks: before an agent may trade, it must finish a verifiable delay function, a sequential puzzle taking about two hours of real time that no extra machines can speed up. Like a willow that bends but cannot be rushed to grow, the delay is fixed by time, not money. Each forged identity then costs two hours of wall-clock time, so spinning up ten thousand sock puppets takes years of sequential work, while an honest agent pays once and then pulses along with the economy at its normal heartbeat.
